newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh police hold at lest 30 Uighurs-exile group.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh police hold at lest 30 Uighurs-exile group.

text.p: A Uighur exile group said at least 30 ethnic Uighurs were detained by police in the Kazakh capital Almaty on Monday after they demonstrated outside the Chinese embassy over executions in China's Xinjiang province.

"Young Uighurs went to protest outside the Chinese embassy and they have not returned to their homes," Yusupbek Mukhlisi, leader of the United Revolutionary Front of Eastern Turkestan, a Uighur exile group based in Almaty, told Reuters by telephone.
He said at least 30 demonstrators had been detained by Kazakh police and said his son, Mukhiddin, who is also the separatist group's spokesman, was among those detained.
Officials at the Kazakh interior and security ministries said they had no information of any Uighur detentions.
Xinjiang, a remote region of desert and mountains in northwest China that is home to the Uighurs and other Turkic-speaking peoples, has a long history of ethnic friction.
Riots in February in the town of Yining, near the border with Kazakhstan, began as a demonstration for Xinjiang's independence and turned violent, killing nine people and injuring 198.
On Monday, a Xinjiang official said Chinese paramilitary police shot dead two people in the province last week when a mob of more than 100 tried to rescue convicted rioters from execution.
Officials in Xinjiang said three Uighurs were executed last week.
The restive province, bordering Afghanistan, Pakistan and three mostly Moslem Central Asian states, has also been shaken by bombings in recent months.
Kazakhs and Uighurs share a common religious, linguistic and cultural heritage. But the former Soviet republic is under pressure from China to clamp down on the activities of Uighur exile groups.
